newsitem.title: USA: Crestar, Citizens Bancorp sign merger.
newsitem.headline: Crestar, Citizens Bancorp sign merger.

text.p: Crestar Financial Corp and Citizens Bancorp said Monday they have signed a definitive merger agreement, in a transaction valued at an estimated $774 million.
Under the agreement, Citizens' shareholders will receive 0.835 shares of Crestar common stock for each share of Citizens stock they hold.
The merger is expected to be completed by March 31, 1997, after approval by shareholders and regulators.

Based on Crestar's $61.375 per share closing price and 15.1 million Citizens' shares outstanding as of September 13, the transaction is valued at $774 million, or $51.25 per Citizens share, the companies said.
After the merger, Citizens will become part of Crestar.
Based on figures from the 1996 second quarter, the transaction will increase Crestar's total assets by 23 percent, to $22.7 billion, and add "substantially" to its branch network.
Stock buyback plans approved by Crestar on July 11 and by Citizens on August 8 have been terminated immediately.

Richard Tilghman, chairman and chief executive of Crestar, said in a statement that one-time merger costs could hurt Crestar's results for the first quarter of 1997. But, he said, the transaction is expected to boost Crestar's earnings during the remainder of the year.
William Harris, chairman of Crestar's Greater Washington and Maryland Banking Group, said an unspecified number of branches will close as a result of the merger.
